plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE with effect-size gating
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single gene-level Salmon count matrix (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 120 samples, first column gene symbol) with a 120-row metadata table carrying one condition column: 60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired human whole blood, single batch. The research question has two parts — which genes differ, and which differences are large enough to matter — so the plan separates a significance test from an explicit effect-size test rather than post-hoc filtering a fold change.

Method choice is driven by the cohort size. With 60 per group this is a population-scale cohort, where the negative-binomial models (DESeq2, edgeR) are documented to exaggerate false positives even on permuted labels (Li et al. 2022, Genome Biology 23:79). The primary test is therefore limma-voom with TMM normalization and a fixed-effects linear model on ~condition, with filterByExpr applied before voom so the mean-variance trend is not distorted by near-zero genes. Because that paper recommends a rank-based test at this sample size, a Wilcoxon rank-sum test on log-CPM is run as an independent control and the overlap with the voom calls is reported — the honest reading of the primary list is the intersection.

The 'large enough to matter' half of the question is answered inside the model, not by filtering afterwards: treat() / TREAT tests each gene against a stated log2 fold-change threshold (1.0 primary, 0.585 secondary as sensitivity), which keeps FDR control for the threshold question, whereas selecting padj<0.05 then |log2FC|>1 does not. Both the unshrunken log2FC with its standard error and confidence interval and the moderated t statistic are carried into the results table, and the significant set is sorted by effect size, not by p-value.

Step 1 is the pre-model QC required on any count matrix: blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library-size distribution — this is where an outlier sample or an unlabelled structural split (the only batch information available is 'single batch', which the profile asserts but cannot verify) would surface before any test is fitted. Step 4 is an optional interpretive layer: over-representation of the effect-size-passing genes against human WikiPathways, which is present in the reference store, with the tested genes as the universe. It enriches the answer but is not required by it; if the pathway resource is unavailable the step reports that and the DE answer stands.

No drug, biomarker, outcome, or safety variable exists in this metadata (one condition column only), so no translational or predictive-modeling steps are planned — they would be unasked scope.
